  <section v="9">

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the ultimate purpose of creation is not for the higher worlds but for the lower world, where through transforming folly and darkness one makes a dwelling place for the Essence of the Ein Sof.

translations.translation: Now, not only according to the opinion
that the Tzemach Tzedek brings,
that even the vessels of Atzilus are a revelation of the concealment,
for according to this opinion certainly the intention is not for Atzilus, since this is a descent and only revelations,
but even according to the second opinion that he brings there, that the vessels are a creation of yesh mei’ayin,
it is explained in many places
that when we say the vessels are a creation of yesh mei’ayin, the intention is not a literal yesh mei’ayin,
rather this is only relative to the light,
because the source of the vessels is from the reshimah, which is a state of concealment, and therefore their existence is also in a manner that their origin is in concealment,
and therefore relative to the light they are like a creation of yesh mei’ayin,
but relative to the reshimah they are a revelation of the concealment.
Thus, it is understood that the intention is not the upper worlds, but rather the service in this lower world of itkafya and it’hapcha.
And even though now, through the performance of mitzvos, we add lights in Atzilus,
and if so, how can we say that even now the main intention is specifically this lower world?
To this, the Rebbe Maharash explains
that these lights in Atzilus are there like something placed in a box,
because they are not for the sake of Atzilus,
but rather for the need of the lower world, and they are not revealed in Atzilus.
And this is what the Rebbe, of blessed memory, explains
regarding the matter that it is impossible to say that the intention is for the upper worlds, since for them it is a descent from the light of His countenance,
that the explanation of this is that the upper worlds are matters of revelation, which is a descent, and also that the Awtsmoos is separate from the matter of revelations,
rather the ultimate purpose is this lower world,
for so it arose in His will, to have gratification before Him when the sitra achra is subdued
and darkness is transformed into light,
and as is explained in the maamar,
that all the service is to transform the folly of the side of impurity into the folly of holiness,
and through this there is gratification before Him, “I said and My will was done,”
and through this they draw down that He should have a dwelling place in the lower realms,
and just as in a dwelling, a person dwells in it with all his essence and being,
so too is it in the lower realms, that they are a dwelling place for Him,
meaning that they draw down not only revelations, but rather the Essence of Ein Sof, blessed is He, is found in them.
And this is the ultimate purpose of the creation and the chain of descent of the worlds.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section illustrates how the Rebbes personally fulfilled the service of transforming folly and selflessly devoted themselves to others, serving as examples for their followers.

translations.translation: Now, at the conclusion of the maamar,
it is explained,
that because the main dwelling of the Shechinah is in the lower realms,
the main revelation of this was in the Holy Temple,
this is the reason that the Mishkan was specifically made of shittim wood,
because the intention is to transform the folly of the side of impurity and the agitation of the animal soul into the folly of holiness,
and as our sages said,
“His folly helped the elder,”
service and self-nullification that are above reason and intellect.
Now, all the matters that were demanded of us by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, and likewise the other Nesi’im, they themselves fulfilled,
and this is in the manner of our sages’ explanation of the verse,
“He declares His words to Yaakov, His statutes and judgments to Israel,” that what He does, He tells Israel to do and to observe,
and likewise, what He commands Israel, He does,
and so it is with the instructions of our Nesi’im, that what they demanded of those connected and belonging to them, they themselves fulfilled and did so.
And what they revealed to us that they fulfilled this,
is so that it would be easier for us to fulfill them.
And so it is with the matter of Ahavas Yisrael, about which there are many stories from each of the Nesi’im.
For example, from the Alter Rebbe, who interrupted his prayer and went to chop wood, cook soup, and personally feed a woman who had just given birth,
because there were no other people in the house.
From the Mitteler Rebbe,
how someone came to him for yechidus and complained about the matters that young married scholars complain about.
And the Mitteler Rebbe bared his arm and said to him, “Do you not see that my skin has shriveled upon me?”
“And all this is from your vitality.”
From this one understands the wonder and exalted level of the Mitteler Rebbe in general, and particularly regarding those matters that are related to such things,
and nevertheless, his connection with them was so great that from their matters, which were not as they should be,
it caused him extreme physical weakness,
until his skin shriveled upon him.
From the Tzemach Tzedek,
how before prayer he went to accompany a gemach for a simple person, which affected his livelihood.
From the Rebbe Maharash,
that once
he traveled specifically from Koharart to Paris and met there with a young married scholar and told him: “Young man, yeyn nesech dulls the mind and heart,
be a Jew.”
And the young scholar went home,
and was not at rest until he came to the Rebbe Maharash,
repented, and from him emerged a family of G-d-fearing and pious people.
It is known that for the Rebbe Maharash, time was extremely precious,
to the extent that even the delivery of Chassidus was brief,
and at certain times, by the eighth hour in the morning he was already after prayer,
and nevertheless, he traveled a distant journey and stayed there for a length of time for the sake of a young scholar, etc.
From the Rebbe, of blessed memory, at the beginning of his leadership,
when a new decree was then decreed and he needed to travel regarding this to Moscow.
And his older brother, the Raza, of blessed memory, said to him,
“Your time is precious and you do not know the language of the country well”
(the Raza was learned in languages)
“and you also need to seek acquaintances,
therefore I will travel regarding this matter according to your instructions.”
But the Rebbe, of blessed memory, did not agree to this and traveled himself and succeeded.
And likewise there are several stories about my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, regarding his efforts to do good, even for a private individual,
whether spiritually or physically.
And he devoted himself to this,
not only his physical being but also his spiritual being,
even though the one he was benefiting was not only not in the category of “your friend in Torah and mitzvos,”
but was completely incomparable to him.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through itkafya and it’hapcha, a dwelling place is made in the lower realms on a higher level than before the sin, and the service of the seventh generation is to draw down the Shechinah below by transforming the folly of the animal soul.

translations.translation: Now, through itkafya and it’hapcha into the folly of holiness, through this the purpose of creation is fulfilled,
which is that He should have a dwelling place in the lower realms,
and this, that through itkafya and it’hapcha a dwelling place is made in the lower realms,
“I have come to My garden,”
is on a more elevated level than before the sin.
For just as when one demolishes a previous building in order to rebuild,
it is obvious that the new building must be on a more elevated level than the previous building,
so too it must be said that through itkafya and it’hapcha a dwelling place is made on a more elevated level,
and as is explained in the maamar,
that through the subduing of the sitra achra, “the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated throughout all the worlds,”
meaning the light that is in all the worlds equally.
And even though the language in the maamar is “the light that encompasses all worlds,”
nevertheless, it is impossible to say that the intention is that a light is drawn down that is within the category of the worlds, but rather it encompasses and surrounds them,
rather the intention is that a supernal light is drawn down that is not within the category of worlds at all.
Therefore, the revelation of this light is called “elevation.”
And therefore, the passing of tzaddikim is also called “elevation,”
because elevation is the revelation of a most supernal light.
For there are two letters in Igeres HaKodesh
that explain the matter of elevation.
And in the second letter, the matter of elevation is explained there regarding the matter of the red heifer.
For the matters done inside cannot refine the most severe impurity,
rather only a matter done outside specifically,
the heifer done outside.
And to this the death of tzaddikim is compared.
Now, there is no red heifer now,
for because of our sins it was necessary that we be exiled from our land,
but the passing of tzaddikim occurred.
And regarding the matter of the passing of tzaddikim, there are two statements of our sages:
“The death of tzaddikim is equivalent to the burning of the house of our G-d.”
“The passing of tzaddikim is more difficult than the destruction of the Holy Temple.”
Through all this, “the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated.”
And the explanation of the matter of elevation was explained by all the Rebbes,
the Alter Rebbe,
the Mitteler Rebbe,
the Tzemach Tzedek,
the Rebbe Maharash,
the Rebbe, of blessed memory, and my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe,
that the intention in the explanation of the word “elevation” is not that it is an ascent above, heaven forbid,
rather the intention is that he is found below, but in a state of loftiness.
And this is demanded of us,
the seventh generation from the Alter Rebbe,
and all sevenths are beloved,
that even though one has not merited it and has not labored for it,
nevertheless, all sevenths are beloved, and the service of the seventh generation is to draw down the Shechinah below, literally.
To transform the folly of the animal soul,
which a person knows in himself that he has it,
and the agitation of the animal soul that he has it, and perhaps sometimes even lower,
to make from this and transform this into the folly of holiness.
